\section*{Executive abstract}
Raw-timestream conditioning is a scientific method, not merely a sequence of
array operations. Despiking decides which measurements are inconsistent with
an intended signal model. Donor replacement redistributes information between
detectors or times. Notches and broad-band filters remove temporal modes and
alter amplitude, phase, support, and covariance. Decimation changes temporal
identity and can alias rejected modes into the retained band. Each choice can
therefore change a point-source peak, effective PSF, centroid, extended-source
response, calibration transfer, or scientific eligibility without changing a
unit label.

SCI-RTC v0.1/r0.3 organizes those choices as \textbf{learn--resolve--apply}.
Learn uses a declared population and diagnostics to estimate candidate
parameters and uncertainty. Resolve combines that evidence with fixed policy
and admits one complete immutable RTC plan. Apply executes exactly that plan
and does not relearn or retune. An online adaptive filter is a different,
time-varying estimator and remains unavailable unless separately authorized.
Missing evidence or tolerances are not passes.

Each resolved response is evaluated against the astronomical temporal
spectrum induced by the realized scan velocity, projected beam, source class,
cadence, and preceding response. A fixed cutoff is not equally safe for all
scan speeds or directions. A notch that removes an interference line also
removes whatever astronomical response lies in its width. A detector-static
\texttt{flxscale} cannot restore removed temporal modes, and calibration
transfer across different RTC plans requires explicit response accounting or
observational evidence.

The output is an atomic bundle of signal, exact plan identity, response,
timing convention, support, influence, validity, uncertainty status, and
provenance. When a required predicate is unresolved, the affected operation
or claim is explicitly unavailable. The formal appendices are the sole
normative authority; Sections 1--12 explain their scientific meaning.

\RationaleBox{Reading rule.}{Narrative text explains the shared authority but
cannot weaken a requirement, choose a missing numerical value, or convert an
unavailable state into a pass.}

\section{Executive summary and present status}
\label{sec:rat-summary}
RTC is the scientific transformation between an admitted aligned detector
stream and a conditioned stream whose temporal and detector-mixing response
is explicit. Its purpose is not to make every sample finite or every spectrum
smooth. Its purpose is to address declared contamination and sampling
problems while preserving a quantitatively adequate response for the intended
astronomical estimator.

The v0.1 scientific method is learned-then-fixed. Evidence may be learned from
a declared population, but application begins only after resolve has produced
one complete immutable plan. Online adaptation is a different estimator and
is unavailable in this revision. Fixed plans use the same resolve and apply
discipline even when no parameter is learned from the observation.

Every operation is interpreted through ten questions: purpose, signal model,
operator, design parameters, learning, resolution and application,
astronomical consequences, calibration consequences, validation, and
unavailable states. Those questions are applied below to despiking, donors,
masks, notches, broad-band and general filters, state, boundaries, non-finite
handling, and decimation.

The current document is a draft for scientific-owner review. It establishes
no production numbers. Open decisions remain open in the ledger; their
dependent operations are unavailable. The formal core defines algebraic and
semantic authority only. Implementation conformity, representation fidelity,
observational performance, science qualification, and production readiness
are explicitly unassessed.

\RationaleBox{Present decision boundary.}{The owner is being asked to approve
the scientific architecture and later resolve the enumerated numerical and
policy choices---not to infer those choices from current software or historical
practice.}

\clearpage
\section{The learn--resolve--apply paradigm}
\label{sec:rat-lifecycle}
RTC begins with a scientific question: which contaminant or sampling problem
must be addressed while retaining adequate astronomical response? The answer
is not an operation name. It is a lifecycle that identifies evidence,
converts it into a fully specified plan, and applies that plan without hidden
adaptation.

\textbf{Learn.} Learn uses a declared population: a separate training
interval, a designated part of the same observation, a collection of scans,
an observation aggregate, or another named population. It may estimate spike
statistics, line centers and widths, filter bands, tap candidates, masks, scan
classes, decimation candidates, donor groupings, quality, and uncertainty.
Each diagnostic carries estimator, unit, support, selection, and failure
state. Learning from the observation later conditioned makes the operator
data-dependent. Conditional linear response at fixed state does not eliminate
selection bias or parameter-estimation uncertainty.

\textbf{Resolve.} Resolve combines evidence with owner-approved policy. It
accepts or rejects every scientific predicate and produces one immutable plan
containing sequence, coefficient identity, rates and conventions, order,
bands and tolerances, notch state, applicability, masks, donor policy, edges,
guards, resets, decimation phase, output timing, expected response/support,
uncertainty, and downstream compatibility. Missing evidence or tolerance
leaves the dependent plan unresolved.

\textbf{Apply.} Apply consumes exactly one resolved plan. It does not move a
notch, change a cutoff or tap count, switch donor policy, change decimation,
silently fall back, or refit a parameter. Restart restores the same plan and
rejects incompatible inputs. Realized state records what ran without rewriting
the request or resolved plan.

V0.1 also permits \textbf{bounded iterative notch-plan refinement}.  This is
an outer finite sequence of complete learn--resolve--apply cycles. Parameters
may change only after one apply has finished and a successor learn and resolve
have admitted a new complete plan. Each apply remains immutable. This is the
v0.1 scientific meaning when ``adaptive notch'' is used; it is not continuous
coefficient tracking and is not the online-adaptive estimator of
SCI-RTC-DEF-025.

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance=0.22in]
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.05in] (input) {original\\input $x^{(0)}$};
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.12in,right=of input] (c1) {\textbf{cycle 1}\\learn $\to$ resolve\\$\to$ immutable apply};
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.02in,right=of c1] (eval) {evaluate\\response +\\diagnostics};
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.12in,right=of eval] (c2) {\textbf{optional cycle 2}\\new learn/resolve\\immutable apply};
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.12in,right=of c2] (final) {final plan $\Pi_K$\\replayed on\\$x^{(0)}$};
\draw[rtcarr] (input)--(c1);
\draw[rtcarr] (c1)--(eval);
\draw[rtcarr] (eval)--(c2);
\draw[rtcarr] (c2)--(final);
\draw[rtcarr,dashed,RTCgold] (eval.south) to[bend right=30]
 node[below,align=center,text=RTCgold]{stop with last accepted plan if no successor passes} (final.south);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

Cycle $k$ learns from an exact population and an evaluation product, resolves
one complete cumulative plan $\Pi_k$, and normally applies that plan to the
original input $x^{(0)}$. A successor plan names all retained, modified,
removed, or rejected notches and every broad-band, state, mask, edge, timing,
and decimation choice. It is never merely ``add this notch to whatever ran
before.'' The final production product normally replays $\Pi_K$ against the
original input, avoiding unintended repeated rounding, padding, state
transients, duplicate filtering, stale masks, or ambiguous parentage.

A sequential cascade from the preceding filtered product is a different
scientific operator. It is allowed only when selected explicitly and when
every immutable intermediate parent, response, state, phase, support,
covariance, and uncertainty is retained. Learned-then-fixed and online-adaptive
filtering remain different: in the latter, parameters evolve inside one apply
pass. V0.1 does not authorize that branch.

\RationaleBox{Lifecycle test.}{For each cycle identify the learning and parent
products, reproduce every predicate, name the complete cumulative plan, and
show that apply did not modify it. Then identify the finite stop cause and the
final selected plan. If any link is absent, the refinement claim is unavailable.}

\clearpage
\section{Temporal frequencies, scan speed, and astronomical spatial scales}
\label{sec:rat-temporal-spatial}
The same temporal frequency represents different angular structure in
different scans. For a locally Gaussian effective beam with covariance
$\Sigma$ and angular scan velocity $\mathbf v$, the characteristic crossing
time is equation~\eqref{eq:crossing-time}. It uses the beam projected along
the actual scan direction, not merely a scalar array FWHM. Source extent,
detector and telescope response, prior RTC stages, and cadence further shape
the exact source-times-response spectrum.

High frequencies correspond to finer scan-direction structure. Low
frequencies contain broad sky structure together with baselines, atmosphere,
and slow instrumental behavior. These do not cleanly separate source and
contaminant. A Gaussian is not band-limited; extended emission can share low
frequencies with atmosphere; a coherent line can overlap a source crossing.
The shorthand $f\sim v/\theta$ is pedagogical only.

\draw[->,thick] (0,0)--(7.5,0) node[right]{frequency};
\draw[->,thick] (0,0)--(0,3.45) node[above]{response};
\draw[RTCblue,very thick,smooth] plot coordinates
 {(0,3)(1,2.9)(2,2.55)(3,1.8)(4,0.9)(5,0.3)(6.5,0.03)};
\draw[RTCgold,very thick] (3.4,0)--(3.4,3.1);
\draw[RTCgray,very thick] (0,2.72)--(4.3,2.72)--(5.6,0.25)--(7,0.25);
\node[RTCblue,align=center] at (5.25,1.05){source-crossing\\spectrum};
\node[RTCgold] at (3.4,3.28){notch};

\node[align=center] at (5.9,-0.55){fine scan structure};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

Changing speed moves astronomical modes relative to a fixed cutoff or notch;
changing direction changes projected beam width. Every filter is assessed
over declared speed, direction, beam, source extent, and source class using
the exact realized response. Preserved dimensions or units do not establish
preserved peak, PSF, centroid, extended response, or absolute mode.

\clearpage
\section{Despiking and donor replacement}
\label{sec:rat-despike-donor}
\textbf{Despike purpose and model.} Despiking identifies samples inconsistent
with an intended detector-plus-sky signal under a stated contaminant model.
The statistic, baseline, threshold, support, mask, and false-positive control
define the method. Learn may estimate statistics from a declared population;
resolve freezes the estimator, threshold, support, boundaries and
disposition; apply evaluates them unchanged. A false positive removes sky
signal, while a false negative can ring through a long filter. Convergence of
an optimizer is not evidence of unbiased retained signal.

A \textbf{donor} is an admitted detector-time measurement used to construct a
continuity surrogate for a rejected target cell. The output remains located
at the target detector and time, but its numerical information comes partly
or wholly from the donor. This can prevent a spike, NaN, or gap from
contaminating a later filter; it is not automatically reconstruction of the
missing astronomical measurement.

Donor and target can differ in focal-plane position, instantaneous sky,
beam, atmosphere coupling, baseline, electronic response, loading, noise, and
covariance. Numerical convention transfer, donor admissibility, and
scientific eligibility are distinct questions. Under $z_i=\phi_i x_i$,
equation~\eqref{eq:raw-donor} uses $\phi_q/\phi_d$ only for exact compatible
occurrences with nonzero target factor. The ratio solves a raw-domain
convention problem; it does not prove that both detectors observed the same
sky. Beammap donor factors must come from an identified prior APT or other
pre-existing authority, never the new \texttt{flxscale} being derived from
that same Beammap.

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance=0.55in]
\node[rtcbox] (t) {target $(d,j)$\\rejected value\\retains identity};
\node[rtcbox,above right=0.12in and 0.92in of t] (d) {donor $(q,\ell)$\\distinct measurement\\distinct sky support};
\node[rtcbox,below right=0.12in and 0.92in of t] (o) {continuity surrogate\\target location\\donor information};
\draw[rtcarr] (d)--node[right,align=left]{admissibility +\\domain transfer}(o);
\draw[rtcarr] (t)--node[below,align=center]{identity + cause}(o);
\node[draw=RTCgold,dashed,rounded corners,fit=(t)(d)(o),inner sep=6pt,
 label={[text=RTCgold]below:support, response, and covariance retain every link}]{};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

Resolve selects topology, time relation, masks, quality, scoring, ties,
weights, baseline treatment, reuse and fallback. Apply cannot change them.
Reused donors create correlations and no exposure. V0.1 retains the selected
conservative policy: every output transitively influenced by RTC replacement
or ALIGN synthesis is scientifically ineligible, while value, cause,
response, and support remain visible. Validation injects spikes, invalid
samples, factor differences, sky mismatch, donor reuse, source crossings and
mask-edge cases, measuring bias, covariance, affected support and data loss.

\clearpage
\section{Notch filtering and learned interference removal}
\label{sec:rat-notch}
A notch suppresses a narrowband coherent disturbance while preserving as much
surrounding astronomical information as possible. A line's physical origin is
not inferred from frequency or coherence. The scientific question is what
astronomical transfer, phase, support and covariance remain, not only whether
the line disappeared.

A resolved notch declares center, rate and frequency convention, width or Q,
depth, family and order, poles/zeros where applicable, phase and group delay,
state, transient and guard, applicability, learned uncertainty, and drift
tolerance. Equation~\eqref{eq:notch-response} is a generic pole-zero form; the
exact realized transfer is authoritative. A too-narrow notch leaves a drifting
or finite-width line; a broad notch removes more sky and noise. High Q usually
means longer memory. Greater depth can increase numerical sensitivity.
Forward/backward use changes magnitude, order, phase and boundaries.
Overlapping notches require combined-response analysis.

Learn defines detection, parameter estimation, significance, false-detection
control, and the declared detector, network, array, and scan scope. Resolve
freezes a common plan
and its drift-validity domain. Apply uses it unchanged. A line not found in
learn does not prove absence in apply; fitting noise can remove real sky
modes. An evolving notch is an online-adaptive estimator with separate update,
response, stability and restart authority; it remains unavailable in v0.1.

\textbf{Successor-cycle assessment.} A later learn pass first asks whether the
accepted plan had its intended consequences: line attenuation and residual
significance, center error or drift, adequate width/depth, ringing, transient,
stability, edge loss, phase and group delay, point-source amplitude and
centroid, effective PSF, extended-source transfer, covariance, and support.
On a declared fixed-state LTI interior, the predicted filtered PSD may be
compared with $P_{\mathrm{pred},k}(f)=|H_k(f)|^2P_0(f)$. That diagnostic is not
universal at masks, edges, state transitions, selections, or nonstationary
intervals. The spectral hole made by a notch is expected filter response, not
new evidence that the original disturbance was absent.

The second question is whether conditioned diagnostics warrant a successor
notch. A peak is not sufficient. Resolve compares original, predicted, and
conditioned PSDs; cumulative response; line uncertainty; astronomical temporal
spectrum; transfer and alias budgets; and detector/network/array/scan/interval
consistency. It rejects notch-edge artifacts, ringing, transients, leakage,
normalization changes, numerical features, and structure where response is too
small for inference. Held-out scans are preferred where practical. Reusing the
same data for selection and assessment is labeled observation-internal,
data-dependent consistency, not independent validation.

\textbf{Bounded admission and stopping.} A successor is admitted only when its
line and parameters are identifiable, it improves the interference metric,
and cumulative astronomical amplitude, centroid, PSF, phase, registration,
ringing, stability, support, cadence, response, uncertainty, and provenance
budgets all pass. Missing evidence or tolerance is not a pass. Rejection leaves
the last accepted plan available and preserves the proposal and cause.
Iteration stops under an owner-approved finite policy governing cycle count,
notch count, removed bandwidth, scientific loss, delay, ringing, edge loss,
minimum improvement, plan stability, false-line control, and fallback.
Maximum-cycle termination is not convergence. Alternating line sets or
unstable parameters are explicitly nonconvergent.

\textbf{Example.} Cycle 1 learns a strong coherent line and resolves a notch.
After immutable apply, Cycle 2 learns from its diagnostic product and reveals
a weaker line. It resolves a complete two-notch plan, which is replayed once
against the original input. In the counterexample, a peak at the first notch
edge agrees with predicted ringing or response artifact; the candidate is
rejected and the one-notch plan remains final. More notches are not
automatically better.

\texttt{flxscale} cannot restore removed frequencies. Beammap and science
observations with different notch plans do not automatically share
point-source response, even under the same label. Validation varies center
error, drift, width, depth, Q/order, state, direction and overlap, measuring
residual line, source transfer, ringing, transient, amplitude, centroid,
covariance and edge loss.

\clearpage
\section{Low-pass, high-pass, and band-pass filtering}
\label{sec:rat-bands}
\textbf{Low-pass.} A low-pass suppresses frequencies above a declared band.
It can reduce high-frequency noise, prepare for decimation, control aliasing,
or define a retained band. It can also attenuate a fast source crossing,
broaden or shift the PSF, reduce peak, alter morphology, ring, increase
covariance, and reduce usable edge support. Its plan states passband and
stopband edges, transition width, ripple, attenuation, phase/delay, family,
taps/order, precision, edges and guards.

\textbf{High-pass.} A high-pass can suppress drift or broad atmosphere, but
also removes large angular scales, extended flux, absolute or slow sky modes,
beam wings and baselines. It can generate negative lobes around compact
sources. Any admitted branch needs an explicit recoverable-mode statement.

\textbf{Band-pass.} A band-pass defines a finite scan-dependent temporal and
spatial band. Both rejected ends require justification; its combined
response, not two cutoff labels, is authoritative.

V0.1 admits these classes only through a resolved selected policy and chooses
no universal cutoff or family. Where no role is named, the branch is
unavailable. Studies vary edges, ripple, attenuation, family, precision,
speed, projected beam and source extent, measuring point and extended
response, ringing, delay, covariance and usable fraction.

\clearpage
\section{Filter order, tap count, phase, and temporal registration}
\label{sec:rat-order-phase}
FIR tap count is a scientific design result, not an arbitrary integer.
Equation~\eqref{eq:fir-order-selection} chooses the smallest order satisfying
passband, stopband, phase, alias, edge and realizability requirements. A
window estimate can initialize a search; only exact coefficients and response
close the predicates.

More taps can sharpen transition or attenuation, but increase computation,
support, covariance footprint, affected outputs after replacement, and edge
loss. They can ring around sources and spikes. Quantization can degrade
ripple, attenuation, notch placement and stability. A causal linear-phase FIR
has equation~\eqref{eq:fir-group-delay}; forward/backward use can remove ideal
interior phase while squaring magnitude, doubling effective order and changing
boundaries.

Delay creates scan-direction displacement by equation~\eqref{eq:scan-displacement}.
The output grid time can be simple while response is centered elsewhere.
Beammap and Pointing are especially sensitive. Resolve requires zero phase, a
shifted time, coordinate correction, response-aware estimator, or a bound
showing residual position and PSF effect is negligible.

\end{tikzpicture}

Validation varies taps, family, precision, bands, speed, beam and source class,
measuring amplitude, shape, delay, ringing, aliasing, covariance, coordinate
registration and usable length. Coefficient algebra alone is not science
qualification.

\clearpage
\section{Decimation and alias control}
\label{sec:rat-decimation}
V0.1 phase-zero downsampling, equation~\eqref{eq:phase-zero}, is point
selection $u[Mn]$, not averaging and not anti-alias filtering. It changes
software cadence, Nyquist frequency, temporal identity, support, covariance,
aliasing, and coordinate registration. The preceding filter determines the
rejected-band power that remains to fold.

Equation~\eqref{eq:alias} shows that components separated by integer multiples
of output rate can appear at the same output frequency. Before resolving $M$,
the exact prefilter must meet approved tolerances in all folded bands and the
declared source domain. A Gaussian is not band-limited, so ``safe'' means
bounded residual transfer and alias, not exact preservation.

Factor choice uses input cadence, exact prefilter, bands, smallest projected
beam-crossing time, maximum valid scan speed, source class, required output
cadence, delay/coordinate accuracy and consumer compatibility.

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance=0.24in]
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.28in] (i) {input spectrum\\sky + noise + lines};
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.28in,right=of i] (p) {exact prefilter\\bounded bands};
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.28in,right=of p] (s) {phase-zero\\$u[Mn]$};
\node[rtcbox,text width=1.28in,right=of s] (o) {output\\folded images};
\draw[rtcarr](i)--(p);\draw[rtcarr](p)--(s);\draw[rtcarr](s)--(o);
\draw[rtcarr,dashed,RTCgold] (p.south) to[bend right=28]
 node[below,align=center,text=RTCgold]{inadequate rejection returns as alias}(o.south);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

Selected grid time $t_{Mn}$ does not erase preceding delay or broad support.
Science may require zero phase, shifted time, coordinate correction,
response-aware estimation, or a negligibility bound. Tests include on/off-bin
tones, varied scan speeds/directions, smallest-beam sources, delay and
coordinate checks, aliases, incomplete strides, edges and resets.

\clearpage
\section{Masks, edges, state, and non-finite handling}
\label{sec:rat-masks-state}
\textbf{Masks.} A source mask protects a coordinate region or changes data
used to learn an operation. It requires exact frame, topology, binding,
support, validity, geometry, dilation and boundary. It is not acquisition
validity or confidence. It can protect real sources while allowing spikes
inside the region, and can change normalization, create discontinuities or
ringing, and alter state. Learn, resolve and apply state whether the mask is
learned, fixed or consumed and what happens if coordinates are unavailable.

\textbf{FIR boundaries.} Complete-context rejection, zero padding,
reflection, extension and local renormalization are different operators. A
guard removes outputs; it does not prove a residual IIR tail negligible
without a criterion. Short and empty scans need explicit dispositions.

\textbf{IIR state and non-finite values.} A plan states initialization,
reset/carry boundaries, stability, transient, gaps and cross-scan or
cross-observation behavior. A non-finite input can poison state until declared
reset or recovery and cannot silently become zero. Learn may estimate state or
settling; resolve freezes the convention; apply records actual boundaries and
rejects incompatible continuation. Tests place impulses, sources, masks and
NaNs at every boundary and split/rejoin streams at state boundaries.

\clearpage
\section{Calibration, Beammap response, and downstream interpretation}
\label{sec:rat-calibration}
RTC distinguishes detector-static \texttt{flxscale}, sample-dependent target
atmosphere correction, detector mixing, single-detector temporal filters, and
data-dependent learned or adaptive operators. Their order is not chosen by
convenience.

A static factor can commute with a fixed single-detector linear filter on a
common support. It does not generally commute with detector mixing. A
sample-dependent atmosphere operator does not generally commute even with a
single-detector temporal filter. Equation~\eqref{eq:order-equivalence} states
the burden for an alternative. Unresolved order remains a cross-package owner
decision.

Filtering can preserve units while changing peak, PSF, extended response,
phase, centroid and covariance. Calibration does not restore removed modes. A
Beammap-derived \texttt{flxscale} belongs to its complete RTC lineage. A
target with a different RTC plan can have a different point-source transfer.
Names such as ``low-pass'' or ``notch'' are not compatibility: coefficients,
rate, phase, state, masks, edges, decimation and response must agree or be
accounted for.

Cross-plan calibration needs response calculation, declared renormalization,
or observational evidence over the intended source and scan domain. The RTC
bundle preserves the plan needed to compare calibrator and target. Without
compatibility, the unit may remain meaningful while the photometric or PSF
claim is unavailable.

\RationaleBox{Beammap circularity guard.}{New \texttt{flxscale} derived from
a Beammap cannot be used as donor scaling inside that same Beammap RTC
lineage; donor factors come from explicit pre-existing authority.}

\clearpage
\section{Covariance, support, and scientific eligibility}
\label{sec:rat-covariance}
Output dependence expands through alignment, donors, taps or state,
boundaries and sampling. Support---not storage shape---governs information flow.
Reused donors correlate targets, overlapping FIRs correlate neighbors, an IIR
links to its state boundary, and decimation erases none of those facts.

At fixed state, equations~\eqref{eq:conditional-mean} and
\eqref{eq:conditional-cov} propagate an admitted mean and covariance through
the same operator. Data-dependent selection or learned parameters add
selection variation and possibly cross terms. Conditioning does not set them
to zero. Unknown covariance is unavailable, not diagonal, white or zero.

Eligibility differs from computability. V0.1 marks every output transitively
influenced by ALIGN synthesis or RTC replacement ineligible while preserving
value, response, cause and support. Downstream roles may add exclusions but
cannot erase causes or strengthen unavailable response. Donor studies must
measure both bias and resulting data loss; changing this conservative policy
requires owner authority.

Response, uncertainty and eligibility accompany signal in the atomic bundle
of equation~\eqref{eq:bundle}. Finite TOD without exact plan, support,
response or typed unavailability, influence and validity is incomplete.

\clearpage
\section{Validation and open owner decisions}
\label{sec:rat-validation}
Algebraic fixtures are necessary but not sufficient. Validation varies the
scientific design choices and measures the observables they can change.

\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}p{0.17\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}X@{}}
\toprule
Study & Variations & Measurements \\
\midrule
Notch & center error, drift, width, depth, Q/order, state, direction, overlap & residual line, sky transfer, ringing, transient, amplitude, centroid, covariance, edge loss \\
FIR/bands & taps, edges, ripple, attenuation, family, precision, speed, beam, source extent & peak/shape, extended transfer, delay, ringing, alias, covariance, usable fraction \\
Donor & spikes, invalids, factors, sky mismatch, noise, reuse, sources, mask edges & stabilization, bias, covariance, influence extent, scientific data loss \\
Decimation & on/off-bin tones, speeds/directions, smallest beam, delay, aliases, strides, resets & retained/aliased transfer, timing, coordinate shift, PSF, support, edges \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Each study preregisters domain, estimator, tolerance and falsifier. Passing
coefficient algebra does not establish science qualification. Observational
performance, science impact and production readiness are separate layers.

The owner ledger retains unresolved authority for learning populations and
freeze points; despike/donor/mask policies; notch and broad-band purpose and
design; filter families, order/taps, tolerances and precision; edges, state and
non-finites; decimation and alias bounds; phase/coordinate registration;
CAL/RTC compatibility; diagnostics; uncertainty; and bundle members. Online
adaptation remains deferred. An open entry blocks only its named operation or
claim and never authorizes a default or silent fallback. Cross-package
follow-up routes CAL, BEAM, AST, PTC, VAL, MAP and filtering questions without
letting RTC assume their answers.

\RationaleBox{Success criterion.}{For every operation, a scientist can
explain purpose, learned evidence, resolved numerical choice, immutable
application, changed astronomical modes, response and calibration effects,
validation evidence, and remaining unavailable claims.}
